messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector roll (yesterday) we're seeing a 7–12% host-side CPU bump on small streaming requests. Latency P50 is OK, but P95 for 64–256 token streams jumped ~30ms. Noticed more time in tokenization + grpc write path. Can we triage?

sana: Seen it too on staging, good catch. I compared p99 traces before/after and tokenization syscalls are spiking. Suspect different kernel choice is enabling slightly larger minibatches at the runtime layer that cause more small-writes downstream.

will: Added flamegraph from a repro run: `https://perf.internal/runs/4765/flame.svg` — top is `tokenize_utf8` -> `memcpy` -> `writev` -> `grpc::Write` chain. KV cache hits dropped ~4% which explains repeated re-tokenization on some flows.

rachel: KV eviction? Any pattern on hot keys/shards?

will: Yeah — the new batching heuristic groups by model variant only and doesn't prioritize KV affinity. Result: fragmented KV cache hit rate when multiplexing requests across kernels.

alex: Repro steps I used (minimal):
```bash
# stress small streaming requests to host proxy
wrk -t4 -c100 -d60s --latency "http://host:8080/gen?model=redwood-small" -s ./scripts/stream-small.lua
```
Also ran `perf record -g` and exported pprof.

sana: I pulled a small `perf top` snippet (symbol collapsed):
```
  18.3% tokenize_utf8
  11.1% grpc::internal::Write
   9.7% memcpy
   6.2% slab_alloc
   4.8% kvcache::lookup
```
Not pretty.

perf-bot: New regression alert: host-ingress-tokenize CPU +9% vs baseline (rolling 7d) — see dashboard /dash/host-parse/regressions

alex: Quick mitigations to try: 1) revert kernel selector patch to confirm regression, 2) bias batching heuristic to prefer KV affinity when multiplexing, 3) micro-opt on tokenization path (avoid extra copy), 4) grpc coalesce small-write windows. Any preferences for order?

rachel: I'd bias batching first (low-risk config). We can flip selector revert if that doesn't help. I can sketch a config flag to prefer sharded affinity: `batcher.prefers_kv_affinity=true` and run canary.

will: I prototyped a tiny change that keeps batches <= 4 concurrent streams for small requests and coalesces socket writes to 8KB before grpc writev. In my local run p95 dropped ~18ms and CPU ~5%. Patch attached: `diff --git a/batcher.cc b/batcher.cc`.

sana: Can you paste the perf before/after numbers?

will: Before: host CPU 72% average, p95 tail +30ms. After change: host CPU 67%, p95 down ~18ms, KV hit rate up 2.5%. Not perfect but promising.

alex: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) we should add a microbenchmark for streaming write coalescing (to avoid regressions), 2) find why KV affinity dropped with selector change — maybe kernel mapping groups more model variants per worker, causing more cross-shard churn.

rachel: On (1). I'll add a test in `eng/runtime/bench/stream_write_coalesce_test.go` that asserts writev calls per request < 3 for small streams.

deploy-bot: roll start: kernel-selector-canary -> infra-canary (id: canary-2026-03-23-01)

alex: If canary goes well we'll enable `batcher.prefers_kv_affinity` cluster-wide. If not, we'll revert the selector change. Can someone volunteer to watch the canary telemetry for the next 2 hours?

will: I'll watch host parse CPU and p95, ping here on any spikes.

sana: I'll instrument KV shard metrics to surface eviction rates per worker and add a short-lived trace to capture tok->write path in production for failing requests.

alex: Thanks — plan sounds good. After we validate, follow-up items: ticket to add automatic fallback to kernel selector that considers KV affinity score; perf task to remove an extra memcpy in `tokenize_utf8` (small but repeated).

rachel: +1, and add a note to release notes about improved small-stream latency if fix ships.

alex: OK closing triage — will update with canary link. :thumbsup:
